name: Hereditary Motor Neuropathy Type V
aliases: Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy Type V

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Criteria for HMN Type V

criteria.description: Presence of distal muscle weakness predominantly affecting the upper limbs
Electrophysiological evidence of motor neuropathy with normal sensory nerve conduction studies
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Distal muscle wasting predominantly in the hands and forearms
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with HMN Type V (e.g., GARS gene)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of distal upper limb muscle weakness and wasting with electrophysiological evidence of motor neuropathy and compatible family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and electrophysiological criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle atrophy of hands and forearms
Absent or reduced deep tendon reflexes in upper limbs

occasional.symptomName: Sensory symptoms such as mild paresthesia

imaging: Muscle MRI may show selective muscle atrophy in distal upper limbs
genetic: Pathogenic variants in GARS gene and other HMN-associated genes
other: Electromyography showing chronic denervation and reinnervation
Nerve conduction studies showing reduced motor amplitudes with normal sensory conduction

distinguishingFeatures: No family history in most cases

references: Reilly MM, Shy ME. Hereditary motor and sensory neuropathies. Neurol Clin. 2009;27(3):619-637.
Rossor AM, Polke JM, Houlden H, Reilly MM. Clinical implications of genetic advances in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013;9(10):562-571.
